s.g: A title indicating great respect, prefixed to the names of Tibetan Buddhists.
One of the edible berries of this plant, from which jam may be produced.
A member of the Pembina Band of Chippewa Indians, a historical band of Chippewa (Ojibwe), originally living along the Red River of the North and its tributaries.
(pharmacology) A drug that targets the programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) receptor, intended for use in treating metastatic melanoma.
A particular drug used in chemotherapy.
A food made from meat which has been dried and beaten into a paste, mixed with berries and rendered fat, and shaped into little patties.
(now rare) A speech or piece of writing that is very condensed, conveying a lot of thought or information in few words.
A savoury fishcake delicacy from Indonesia (Palembang), made of fish, egg, and tapioca usually served with the traditional spice-based broth and sometimes also served with noodles.
(pathology) Any of a group of rare autoimmune blistering skin diseases that superficially resemble pemphigus.
(pathology) A severe autoimmune skin disease characterized by pustules and painful blisters, and which can be fatal.
(zoology, countable) An aphid of genus Pemphigus.

pems.f: (automotive) Initialism of portable emissions measurement system.
